title: Sixteen Leagues and One Mile Stone
subtitle: 数学与测量 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数学与测量（科学与技术·数学与测量）
meta: 主题语境：数学与测量（科学与技术·数学与测量）　|　核心词汇：distance　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 distance 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 the surveyor ① measured a distance that no map in the province would have shown, and he said the measuring was the whole of the survey. The ② distance, meaning the length and not the remoteness, ran sixteen leagues and stayed unpainted on the stone; a distance, he said, is the only thing on a road that is judged by how long it is left unmarked.

Every ③ distance in that survey had the same mile stone at the end of it, and the ④ distance at the end, meaning the one they kept for the coast road and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A distance, his assistant said, is nine parts walking and one part somebody willing to measure; the surveyor said the walking is the part that fills sixteen leagues.

The traveller meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the distance was the whole of the journey, meaning the remoteness and not the length. The ⑥ distance, meaning the remoteness and not any of that, is the only thing in a journey that everybody feels and nobody counts; distance, she said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a length and a remoteness. She said the remoteness is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ distance had become a line in a table, and the table had become an argument about the mile stone. The ⑧ distance of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in July, was one survey and sixteen leagues of walking; distance, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to walk. She said the walking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ distance I remember is the one at the end, which was confirmed in 1969 and is still described as the strangest in the survey. A ⑩ distance, the assistant said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being walked; every distance, she said, is a remoteness that has agreed to look like a length. She said the remoteness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 距离；路程（指测量里量得的那一程）
B. n. 距离（指那段长度本身，与那份遥远相对）
C. 固定搭配：measure a distance 测量一段距离
D. n. 距离（指留给海岸公路用的那一段）
E. n. 距离；间距（抽象总称，指一次测量的全部里程）
F. n. 距离（指表里写到、被列明的那一段）
G. n. 遥远；疏远（指旅途中感受到的那种距离感）
H. n. 遥远（抽象总称，指人人感受到却无人计算的那样）

items.q: measured a distance that no map in the province would have shown
The distance, meaning the length and not the remoteness
the distance was the whole of the journey
the distance had become a line in a table
The distance of the whole thing
A distance, the assistant said in 1971

answers.why: measure a distance 意为“测量一段距离”，1946 年测量员测量了一段全省没有一张地图画得出的距离。
distance 意为“距离”，指那段长度本身而不是那份遥远，它长达十六里格而在里程碑上没有刻字。
distance 意为“距离、路程”，指那次测量里每一段距离，每一段末尾都有同一块里程石。
distance 意为“距离”，指留给海岸公路用的那一段，是唯一有人复核过两次的。
distance 意为“遥远、距离感”，指旅途中感受到的那种，旅行者说这种遥远就是那趟旅程的全部。
distance 意为“遥远”，指人人感受到却无人计算的那样而不是那段长度，是旅程里人人都感受到、却无人计算的东西。
distance 意为“距离”，指表里写到、被列明的那一段，到 1955 年这段距离成了表里的一行。
distance 意为“距离、间距”，测量员七月写道，整件事的里程是一次测量和十六里格的步行。
distance 意为“距离”，我记得的是末尾那一段，1969 年被确认，至今仍被说成测量里最奇的一段。
distance 为抽象总称，助手 1971 年说，一段距离是唯一会因为被走完而变得更好的东西。
